overview: Six-month lean A3 in a 16-bed intensive care unit: an eight-week baseline, value stream mapping with five gemba walks at 07:00, then A3 cycles testing two countermeasures in sequence (removal of the informal approval step for patients who pass the screen, then a shared 08:00 time and hand-off card with respiratory therapy).
population: All eligible ventilated patient-days on continuous sedation from September 2026 to April 2027, about 60 a week.
exposure: Countermeasure 1 from week 3 of the A3: nurses stop sedation after a passed screen without waiting for physician agreement, with a physician informed at rounds. Countermeasure 2 from week 9: shared 08:00 time and a bedside hand-off card for the breathing trial.
procedures: The charge nurse records for each eligible patient-day whether the screen, interruption and breathing trial were completed and the reason if not, on a one-line tally sheet. The facilitator runs the A3 with two bedside nurses, one respiratory therapist and one physician. Self-extubations and agitation needing a bolus during interruptions are recorded from the incident system and the chart. Weekly results are posted on the unit board.

outcomes.name: Completed interruptions
outcomes.measure: Weekly proportion of eligible patient-days with a completed sedation interruption
outcomes.why: The step where the local process fails.

outcomes.name: Paired breathing trials
outcomes.measure: Weekly proportion of eligible patient-days with a breathing trial after a passed interruption
outcomes.why: Shows whether the benefit carries through to breathing trials.

outcomes.name: Self-extubation during interruption
outcomes.measure: Count of self-extubations, plotted as days between events
outcomes.why: The harm nurses fear most (claim c3).

outcomes.name: Agitation needing a bolus
outcomes.measure: Weekly proportion of interruptions with a rescue bolus

outcomes.name: Ventilator days
outcomes.measure: Monthly median ventilator days for patients ventilated more than 48 hours
outcomes.why: The patient benefit that adherence is meant to deliver; descriptive only.

feasibility: The tally sheet takes the charge nurse about five minutes a day; the facilitator's four hours a week cover the A3 meetings; no extra staff.
biasMitigation: Tally sheet completed by the charge nurse from the chart, not by the bedside nurse
Countermeasure dates marked on the charts before the following weeks are viewed
Safety events taken from the incident system as well as the chart

biasFlags.label: Documentation drift
biasFlags.note: Charting of interruptions may improve without practice; spot checks at the bedside twice a week.

biasFlags.label: Case mix change
biasFlags.note: More unstable patients reduce eligibility; eligibility is measured every day.

biasFlags.label: Under-reporting of agitation
biasFlags.note: Rescue boluses are taken from the medication record.

flags: Two balancing measures and one process measure
parsimony.simplestPath: One unit, one primary measure on a run chart, two countermeasures in sequence.

theoreticalFramework: Lean thinking (value stream mapping, gemba walks, A3); no additional framework.
summary: Eight-week baseline then two countermeasures in sequence; completed interruptions as the primary measure with two safety measures.
